PullRequest.Title: Show cached titles on restored chat editor tabs
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #344950

After a window reload, chat editor tabs for non-local sessions (agent host, Copilot CLI, and other contributed session types) showed the generic title "Chat" until they were revealed. Their title is only known once the session is loaded, and `IChatService.getSessionTitle` only knows local sessions.

This change caches each tab's last known title in its serialized editor state. A restored tab shows that title right away. Once the session loads, the live title takes over as before.

- `ChatEditorInput.getKnownTitle()` returns the title `getName()` would show, or `undefined` when only the generic fallback is known.
- `ChatEditorInputSerializer` stores it as the new `IChatEditorOptions.restoredTitle`.
- `getName()` prefers `restoredTitle` over `title.preferred`, because the title the editor was opened with can be stale after a rename.
- `restoredTitle` is a separate option rather than `title.preferred`, because `ChatEditor.setInput` pushes `title.preferred` into the session title of contributed sessions.
- `copy()` (split/duplicate) still opens a new chat without a title.

**Before** (`origin/main`, Code OSS, after Developer: Reload Window; the two background tabs are agent host Copilot sessions):

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed2b57b-907e-4f91-be03-a2514d3aea90)

**After** (this branch, two reloads without revealing the background tabs):

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/861d1ab3-05bd-4950-9d09-f5e9f5dbae5b)

### How to test

1. Open three Copilot (agent host) chats as editor tabs and send a message in each so they get titles.
2. Run Developer: Reload Window, twice.
3. All tabs show their session titles without being revealed.

### Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widgetHosts/editor/chatEditorInput.test.ts`: 58 passing, including a new test for serialize → deserialize → `getName()` of an unresolved agent host session, repeated round trips, the untitled fallback, and `copy()`.
- The same run together with `chatMoveActions.test.ts`, `agentHostChatMoveEditors.test.ts`, and `btwSlashCommand.test.ts`: 104 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint` on the changed files: passed.
- Manual check in Code OSS built from this branch: the screenshots above.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist open chat editor tabs during workbench state save or window shutdown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each editor group synchronously serializes its existing editor inputs before the workbench state can be stored. The changed serializer now resolves one known title and includes it in the same JSON payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize editor state with JSON.stringify, now including restoredTitle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per open serializable chat tab when editor-group state is saved
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor options and resources were serialized and written; the payload omitted the last known title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one title string to the existing synchronous editor-state serialization and storage payload

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold synchronous read and JSON parse of the persisted local chat-session metadata index through getSessionTitle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per ChatSessionStore cache lifetime, then map reads; index is capped at 400 local entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Serializer did not explicitly request the title, although normal tab-label getName calls used the same lookup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can occur during serialization only for an unresolved local session if the metadata index has not already been initialized

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the existing workbench editor-state memento
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing state-save operation containing all editor groups
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor state was already stored without restoredTitle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added title bytes are included in the existing state write; no additional write is issued

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open serializable chat tabs; one title lookup and one additional short string per chat tab. For unresolved local tabs, the first lookup can initialize the session metadata index, which is capped at 400 entries, and subsequent lookups reuse the in-memory index cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialization is synchronous and sequential across editors. There is no newly introduced asynchronous fan-out or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved models and active sessions are checked first. Unresolved local sessions use a synchronously cached metadata index; a cold cache parses the bounded index once, while warm lookups are map reads. Non-local sessions do not consult that index. restoredTitle is replaced rather than accumulated on each serialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous call path and one-field payload increase; high confidence that no per-tab I/O, IPC, network, filesystem, or subprocess fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact open-tab counts and custom-title lengths vary, but normal titles are small and the local metadata parse is bounded and cached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The incremental CPU/allocation and stored bytes scale linearly with open chat tabs but are small, while the only cold metadata parse is bounded and coalesced by the existing index cache.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a window with unresolved background chat tabs and render their tab labels
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing editor-state JSON is parsed, ChatEditorInput instances are created, and getName serves the tab label. restoredTitle is a direct option read after live model/session lookups fail; background contributed sessions are not loaded to obtain it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse the existing editor-state JSON containing restoredTitle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse per serialized chat editor entry in the existing restore flow
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same entry was parsed without the extra title property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds only the title string's bytes to the existing parse and object revival

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load a contributed or agent-host chat session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for the restored-title label path
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Background sessions also remained unloaded and displayed the fallback title until revealed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the critical path; getKnownTitle only checks synchronous registries/options and does not load the session

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of restored chat tabs and total title bytes present in editor state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Input deserialization and label reads follow the existing editor restore flow; the change does not start parallel session loads or remote requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The serialized title is the warm cache for background tabs. Live model or active-session titles supersede it. Missing titles retain the existing generic fallback without negative-cache retries beyond existing label reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the synchronous implementation and test covering repeated serialize/deserialize without resolving the session.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A user can retain varying numbers of tabs, but each restored title contributes only its string size and no heavy resource is created.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The feature avoids eager session loading and adds only bounded per-tab state and constant-time label selection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Split or duplicate a chat editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: copy creates a new ChatEditorInput with only the existing session-type selection metadata; it does not carry restoredTitle and therefore performs no added persistence or session work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new input per user split/duplicate action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous input construction; no queue, limiter, or parallel boundary work is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cached restored title is intentionally not copied, so no cache growth or invalidation path is added for duplicated editors.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged copy implementation and the added test assertion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for performance; the action creates the same class of input as before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; no new expensive boundary or retained title is introduced on this path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced save, restore, title lookup, and copy paths. The diff adds a single cached title string per serialized chat tab. It does not load sessions, add boundary-call fan-out, create unbounded retention, or introduce meaningful synchronous UI work; the only cold local metadata lookup is capped and cached.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
